newsitem.title: ITALY: RUGBY UNION-ITALY CHANGES LAWS ON FOREIGN PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ITALY CHANGES LAWS ON FOREIGN PLAYERS.

text.p: Italian rugby union will allow more foreigners to play in the domestic league next season while continuing to impose limits on European players, federation president Giancarlo Dondi said on Tuesday.
Dondi said Italian serie A rugby clubs would be allowed two foreign players in the championship instead of only one as under present rules.
"There is a great pressure from the clubs. They want to have more foreign players," he said.
But Dondi added that Italy, unlike other European rugby nations, would continue to consider non-Italian players from within the European Union (EU) as foreign.

He said the recent Bosman ruling, which stipulates there should be no limitation on athletes from the EU signing for other countries within the 15-nation bloc, did not apply to Italian rugby as it was still amateur.
"The Bosman ruling refers to professional leagues. The Italian league has decided to stay amateur," he said.
Dondi added that players with dual nationality who were excluded from playing for Italy because they had previously represented another country would also be considered to be foreign players.
This was to stop clubs becoming too dependent on players of foreign origin who had taken Italian nationality but could not play for the national team.
"We don't want to damage our national team. We don't want too many foreign players taking the position of our players in the domestic league," Dondi said.
Italy, where rugby is a minority sport, wants to be included in the Five Nations' championship following a string of good wins. They beat a depleted French side 40-32 last month.
